IDENTIFICATION: The pair is **Black and White**. The factor −0.9568 is the log-odds coefficient of Black (vs. White) in a logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on race dummies + SES + a race×SES interaction (SES entered uncentered, White as reference). Fitted value: −0.956778, matching −0.9568 to 4 decimals (deviation +0.000022). Direction: Black has the lower BA-completion log-odds relative to White (odds ratio 0.384).

(1) MATCH (race pair, direction, specification):
- Model: Logit(BA_DEGREE_COMPLETED) ~ race dummies + SES + race×SES, n=8,773, reference = White.
- race:Black coefficient = −0.9568 (SE 0.215, z = −4.44, p < 1e-5); this is the Black-vs-White log-odds contrast at the SES main effect. No other (pair, spec) in the searched space matched within ±0.005.

(2) CONTRAST TABLE (full 381-row table saved to contrast_table.csv; key excerpts, log-odds, White reference):
- race only:              Black vs White −1.0057 | Hispanic vs White −0.9241 | Black vs Hispanic −0.0816
- race+SES:               Black vs White −0.8621 | Hispanic vs White −0.7106 | Black vs Hispanic −0.1515
- race+ASVAB:             Black vs White +0.2619 | Hispanic vs White −0.1481
- race+PCTILE:            Black vs White −0.5946 | Hispanic vs White −0.5170
- race+SES+ASVAB+PCTILE:  Black vs White +0.0926 | Hispanic vs White −0.2665
- +FAMSIZE:               Black vs White +0.0380 | Hispanic vs White +0.1589
- +SEX:                   Black vs White +0.1153 | Hispanic vs White −0.2572
- +FAM+SEX:               Black vs White +0.0378 | Hispanic vs White +0.1608
- standardized-predictor ([z]) versions are numerically identical to their raw counterparts (rescaling continuous covariates does not change race dummy coefficients in a logit).
- Interaction probe (race×SES uncentered): Black vs White **−0.9568 (EXACT)**, Hispanic vs White −0.7160, Black vs Hispanic −0.2408; mean/sd-centered interaction versions give −0.9637 (dev −0.0069), i.e., the exact value requires the uncentered parameterization.
- Also evaluated and rejected: 31 covariate-subset main-effect logits, pairwise two-race-only logits, sex-stratified logits, LPM (OLS), probit, average-marginal-effect scales, and race×ASVAB / race×PCTILE / race×FAMSIZE interactions — none within ±0.005.

(3) SENSITIVITY: −0.9568 does NOT appear across several specifications — it is unique to the race+SES+race×SES model with uncentered SES. Among main-effect models the Black-vs-White contrast ranges from −1.006 (unadjusted) to +0.038, and Hispanic-vs-White from −0.924 to +0.161; the unadjusted Hispanic-vs-White value (−0.9241) was the closest non-exact candidate (dev +0.033). The exact reproduction by a single, simple, plausible specification (logit with SES moderation), with deviation 2e-05, identifies the generating analysis with high confidence and confirms the pair is Black vs White rather than Hispanic vs White.

HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded answer): Between Black and White respondents. In a logistic model of BA degree completion on race, SES, and a race-by-SES interaction (NLS respondents, n = 8,773; 236 BA completions), the coefficient for Black relative to White is −0.9568 — i.e., at equal SES, Black respondents' odds of completing a BA are e^−0.9568 ≈ 0.38 times (62% lower in log-odds terms than) White respondents' odds. The negative SES gradient for Black respondents is substantially attenuated by the positive Black×SES interaction (+0.761), but the Black-vs-White factor itself is −0.9568.

In a logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on race dummies, SES, and a race-by-SES interaction (NLS, n=8773, White reference), the Black-vs-White coefficient is -0.9568 (fitted -0.956778, OR 0.384): at equal SES, Black respondents have substantially lower log-odds of BA completion than White respondents.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspection: 8773 rows; races White 5337/Black 2113/Hispanic 1323; no missing or zero codes in ASVAB, PERCENTILE, SES, BA (BA is boolean; SES negatives are real standardized values). 2) Descriptives by race and raw BA rates (Black 1.33%, Hispanic 1.44%, White 3.54%); raw log-odds contrasts bracket the target (Black-White -1.006, Hispanic-White -0.924). 3) Specification search: 942 contrasts across 32 covariate-subset logits (unadjusted and standardized), all three reference codings, pairwise two-race logits, sex-stratified fits, LPM, probit, AME scales, and race-by-covariate interactions; compared each log-odds contrast (and odds-ratio/AME scales) to -0.9568 with tolerance +/-0.005. 4) Unique exact match: logit with race + SES + race*SES (uncentered SES), Black vs White = -0.956778 (dev 2.2e-05); no other specification within +/-0.005; closest non-match was race-only Hispanic vs White (-0.9241, dev +0.033).
